sections.heading: 6.1 Effect of the Pitfalls
sections.text: In this section we investigate the impact of the experiments proposed in Section 4.2 on the learning performance of a multimodal neural network. Tab. 1 shows the AULC \mathrm{AULC} of the Random query method in the high-label regime of the synthetic datasets. We further compare the effect of applying ModDrop ( Section 5 ). The following paragraphs discuss the results one by one, based on the pitfalls. P1.1 (Missing) The AULC \mathrm{AULC} achieved when evaluated only on the rare modality is significantly smaller than that obtained on the frequent one. The joint AULC \mathrm{AULC} is close to that achieved on the frequent modality only. Employing ModDrop does not yield substantial differences. P2 & P3.1 (Share) The AULC \mathrm{AULC} when evaluated only on CIFAR-10 is considerably smaller than when only evaluated on MNIST. The joint AULC \mathrm{AULC} is close to the AULC \mathrm{AULC} achieved on MNIST only. Here, applying ModDrop increases the performance on the weak modality while leaving the strong modality unaffected. Though, a significant gap between the weak and the strong modalities’ performances remains. P3.2 (Unique) The modality with all task-relevant information performs substantially better than the one with only partial information. The joint AULC \mathrm{AULC} is similar to that of the modality with full information. In this case, ModDrop significantly improves the AULC \mathrm{AULC} gained in the case of partial task-information. The other modality remains unaffected and a performance gap between both modalities remains. P3.3 (Synergy) The model performs best on modality A, achieving considerably higher scores than using modality B. In contrast to previous situations, the joint AULC \mathrm{AULC} is close to the weak modalities performance. Here, ModDrop harms the overall performance, resulting in significantly lower scores. Summary Across all four experimental settings, modality imbalance consistently emerges: models disproportionately rely on one modality regardless of the information structure. ModDrop mitigates this imbalance in all but the synergy setting, where it is actively harmful, reducing joint performance substantially. Based on these results, further evaluation of the synthetic datasets will use ModDrop for all but the synergy dataset. Table 2 : Query Method Comparison on Synthetic Data. sections.heading: 6.2 Query Method Comparison on Synthetic Data
sections.text: Having investigated the effects of the multimodal pitfalls, we now examine unimodal and multimodal query methods on the synthetic settings ( Table 2 ). Specifically, we study their vulnerability to the pitfalls proposed and assess their relative performance. One by one, we visit each pitfall in the following sections. P1.1 (Missing) KCG , Entropy and BALD show significant gains over competitors in the rare modality setting. However, the benefits are not reliable in the case of KCG . Entropy performs best overall, taking the second place in the mid-label and the first place in the high-label regime. P2 & P3.1 (Share) No method reliably improves the weak modality performance in the share setting. Random performs as well as any specialized strategy. P3.2 (Unique) With respect to the partial information modality, differences emerge in the low- and mid-label settings, where GRACE and KCG perform best. In the high label regime, the scores of all methods converge to similar values with Random leading the comparison. P3.3 (Synergy) Query methods perform similar with KCG achieving the first place in the low- and mid-label regimes. BADGE leads in the high-label setting, suggesting that the relative advantage of different strategies depends on the label budget. No method consistently and substantially outperforms its competitors. Summary Table 3 : Summary of Query Method Rankings on Synthetic Data. In order to compare the query methods, we sum the ranks obtained by the query methods for all datasets. The sum of ranks indicates the overall performance. Lower is better. The best entries are highlighted in bold . Label Regime Query Method BADGE BALD BMMAL Entropy GRACE KCG Random Low 16 22 14 17 15 11 17 Mid 22 21 14 17 17 6 15 High 14 11 15 21 15 20 16 The preceding analysis shows that the imbalances introduced by our pitfalls ( Section 6.1 ) are largely unaddressed by existing query methods, with the exception of P1.1. Furthermore, no single query method consistently outperforms the others across all settings and label regimes. To provide an aggregate view, we report summed ranks across weak-modality evaluations in Table 3 . Overall, KCG achieves the best aggregate rank in the low- and mid-label regimes, but its advantage disappears in the high-label regime, where BALD ranks first. This instability further underscores the absence of a reliable strategy for multimodal AL. Table 4 : Query Method Comparison on Real-World Data.
